ます is a polite verb ending, not used after nouns.
いる means 'to exist' and cannot link a noun predicate.

wrong_choice_explanations: ます is a polite verb ending and attaches to verb stems (行きます), not to a noun; 月曜日ます is ungrammatical, since a noun predicate takes the copula です.
ない is the negative ending used with い-adjectives (高くない, 寒くない) — for a noun predicate the negative is じゃない (e.g. 月曜日じゃないです), so 月曜日ない is not valid Japanese.
でした is the past polite copula; since the sentence is about today, the present です is required.

wrong_choice_explanations: だった is the past plain copula and follows nouns, not い-adjectives — the past of おいしい is おいしかった, not おいしいだった.
だ does not attach to い-adjectives in standard Japanese: おいしいだ is incorrect. After い-adjectives, the polite form simply adds です (おいしいです).
ある means 'to exist' for inanimate things and cannot link an い-adjective to a subject the way です does.

ある means 'exists' for inanimate things — you can say 富士山がある, but ある cannot identify あれ as 富士山 the way the copula does.

wrong_choice_explanations: だ does not attach to い-adjectives in standard Japanese — 暖かいだ is ungrammatical; the polite form of an い-adjective simply adds です (暖かいです).
だった follows nouns and な-adjectives, not い-adjectives — the past of 暖かい is 暖かかった, so 暖かいだった is ungrammatical (polite: 暖かかったです).
